Mortgage rates just hit seven point four percent. Most people blame the Fed, but the Fed doesn't set your mortgage rate. Lenders price thirty-year loans off the ten-year Treasury yield, plus a margin. In October that yield hit its highest level since two thousand two. On a four hundred thousand dollar loan, seven point four percent costs about two hundred eighty dollars more a month than last year's rate. So when the ten-year yield climbs, mortgage rates follow, Fed or no Fed. Follow for more money myths, explained.
